outcome: The automation lane stops telling a worker its binding was wrong when the binding was never the problem: AUTOMATION_BINDING_MISMATCH stops standing for three unrelated failures and a fourth unrelated condition, a refused recovery decision names which field disagreed, and the recovery lane's escalation path becomes usable again - closing sworn#250, where a worker reported copying its binding verbatim, was told the binding mismatched, and could not have been right or wrong because the decide tool has no binding field at all.

exclude: the recovery decision vocabulary and the actions a recovery role may take (ValidateRecoveryDecision's rules are correct; this slice is about how their refusal is reported, not what they permit)
the automation invocation identity derivation itself (automationInvocationID in internal/runtime is the sole producer and stays as it is; this slice does not introduce a second derivation)
the exactly-once accounting that makes a recovery decision callable once (untouched: a worker that is refused legibly must still not get a second decision it did not earn)
the submission and sandbox refusal boundaries (sworn#245 and sworn#251 are the same shape at their own seams and are separate slices in this release)

acceptance.text: One code stops meaning four things. decodeAutomationTerminal's recovery branch (internal/driver/automation.go:777-781) today collapses a JSON decode failure, a ValidateRecoveryDecision failure, and an invocation-id mismatch into a single AUTOMATION_BINDING_MISMATCH, its advisory sibling (:804-806) does the same, and validateAutomationInvocation (:394-396) raises the identical code for a profile-or-model selection mismatch that has nothing to do with a binding. After this slice each of those conditions is distinguishable on the durable record, and a decision refused for its shape is never reported as a binding problem. Pinned by tests over each condition asserting distinct, accurate reporting.

A refused decision names what to change. The refusal a recovery worker receives - fed back as error text at internal/driver/automation.go:718-723 and its native equivalent at native_linux.go:298-308 - names the field or rule that refused, so the sworn#250 worker's position becomes impossible: it reported copying the invocation_id and binding verbatim and being told the binding mismatched, when the decide tool's own schema (swornRecoveryDecisionInputSchema, automation.go:27) admits only schema_version, invocation_id, action and answer with additionalProperties false. It had no binding to copy, and an unrelated shape rule - ask_captain carrying an answer, or resume_worker carrying none (automation.go:184-203) - is the likely refusal it was never told about. Pinned by a test that submits each shape violation and finds the violated rule named.

The identity check says what it actually checks. Validation compares the echoed invocation_id to the process-local copy by string equality and never re-derives it from the binding, so no worker can compute or verify the relationship: the honest report for a mismatch names the echoed identity as wrong, not the binding as mismatched. The duplicate post-hoc check in ValidateAutomationObservation (automation.go:421-426) raises a different code, INVALID_AUTOMATION_OBSERVATION, for the identical condition; after this slice the same condition reports the same way from both sites. Pinned by a test asserting a wrong echoed identity reports identically through the decode path and the observation-validation path.

constraints: Legibility must not widen admission: every decision refused today is still refused, and a worker learning why must never become a worker learning how to get an unearned decision accepted. The exactly-once property of a recovery decision is untouched.

No second derivation of the automation invocation identity is introduced. The defect is that a refusal misnames itself, not that the identity is computed in the wrong place; adding a second producer would create the drift class this project has already paid for repeatedly.
A refusal message quotes rule and field names, never the worker's submitted payload, so the error channel cannot be used as an echo surface.

Existing contract codes remain valid values on the wire. Conditions gain accurate reporting; a caller or classifier that matches on AUTOMATION_BINDING_MISMATCH for a genuine binding mismatch continues to see it.
